prompt_text: All in one fundraising and CRM solution
response_text:
**Top all-in-one fundraising and CRM solutions for nonprofits include Sumac CRM, Bloomerang, DonorPerfect, CharityEngine, and Giveffect, which integrate donor management, campaigns, events, volunteers, and more into single platforms.**[1][3][6]

These tools centralize data to eliminate silos, reduce costs from multiple vendors, and scale with organizational growth, often featuring webforms, automation, reporting, and payment integrations like Stripe or PayPal.[1][2][3]

### Key Options and Features
| Solution | Standout Features | Best For |
|----------|-------------------|----------|
| **Sumac CRM** | Donations, case management, memberships, volunteers, grants, prospecting; embeddable webforms; customizable add-ons.[1] | Organizations needing maximum functionality that grows with them. |
| **Bloomerang (includes Kindful)** | Donor engagement, data segmentation, peer-to-peer/crowdfunding, payment integrations.[1] | Improving messaging and supporter-driven campaigns. |
| **DonorPerfect** | Cloud contact management, monthly giving, event ticketing, annual appeals, strong support.[1] | Small/medium nonprofits focused on donor coordination. |
| **CharityEngine** | 360° donor views, marketing automation, events, advocacy, payments, auctions, volunteers; no extra integrations needed.[3] | Teams tired of juggling multiple systems. |
| **Giveffect** | 10-in-1: CRM, fundraising pages, events/auctions, volunteers, automation, donor history tracking.[1][6] | Automating workflows and deepening supporter relationships. |
| **Neon CRM/NeonOne** | Fundraising, events, memberships, emails, online stores; unlimited forms.[1][2][9] | Growing orgs managing multiple revenue streams. |

Other notable mentions: Salesforce Nonprofit Success Pack for large-scale customization with AI (requires technical setup).[2] Virtuous for responsive fundraising, marketing, and volunteer tools.[7] CiviCRM as a free open-source option (needs dev skills).[2]

Choose based on size, budget, and needs—most offer demos for testing scalability and ease of use.[1][3][5]
